tasks.title: Fix booking overbooking race by wiring lockSeat()
tasks.acceptance: Two concurrent POST /api/bookings for the last seat yield exactly one booking + one rejection; cleanup cron reclaims an abandoned lock within TTL. SCOPE EXTENDED 2026-08-06 by Claude (architecture owner) after the second Type E pass: app/api/webhooks/paymob/route.ts and app/api/cron/cleanup-locks/route.ts are now IN SCOPE. BLOCKING DEFECT to fix: the cron cancels an expired PENDING lock, the seat is resold, then the late Paymob webhook sets status CONFIRMED unconditionally (route.ts:163-171) with no capacity or status re-check -> two confirmed bookings on a one-seat class and the first student has paid. Webhook must re-validate capacity in a serializable transaction and, if no seat remains, flag for refund + alert rather than silently confirm. Also reconsider LOCK_DURATION_MINUTES=10 against real Egyptian bank OTP/3DS latency, and stop abandoned online payments from consuming promo usage. app/classes/[id]/book/page.tsx added so T1-02 can supply real schedule data + session profile defaults, which Codex correctly refused to touch while out of scope. REVIEW ROUND 2 - 2026-08-06, both Type E passes re-run by Claude against 6fc2514. The webhook race IS closed and the refund-queue claim is VERIFIED (conflict path writes status=CANCELLED + paymentStatus=PAID + refundReason, and app/api/admin/refund-requests/route.ts selects exactly refundReason!=null AND paymentStatus=PAID, so these do surface). REFUNDED/PARTIALLY_REFUNDED cannot be downgraded, and promo release is exactly-once across cron + failure webhook (both guarded by count===1). ONE BLOCKER REMAINS: the expired-lock branch never checks capacity. hasValidSeatLock requires lockedUntil > now; when it is false the handler goes straight to conflict and CANCELS a booking the customer has just paid for, WITHOUT asking whether a seat is actually free. A student who clears bank OTP at minute 16 of a 15-minute lock on a class with 49 free seats is cancelled and pushed to manual refund. The TTL was raised to 15 minutes precisely because Egyptian bank OTP is slow, so this path will fire in production. REQUIRED FIX: run the occupied-seat count in BOTH branches and raise a conflict only when capacity is genuinely exceeded; reserve outright refund for the case where the seat is truly gone or the student cancelled deliberately. Note the handler cannot currently distinguish a cron-expired cancellation from a user-initiated one - if that distinction is needed to avoid re-confirming a deliberately cancelled booking, add it explicitly rather than inferring it from status.

tasks.title: Close the same overbooking race on the mobile booking path
tasks.acceptance: OPENED 2026-08-06 by Claude on the T1-01 second Type E pass. CONN-001 is only half-closed by T1-01: app/api/mobile/book-class/route.ts still reads _count.bookings (line 34) and compares it to capacity (line 54) OUTSIDE any transaction, then creates the booking - a textbook TOCTOU. Two concurrent mobile bookings for the last seat both pass the check and both write. The web path is now serializable; the mobile path is not, so the overbooking defect remains fully reachable through the app. SECOND, SEPARATE DEFECT: the two paths do not agree on what occupies a seat. Mobile counts every booking with status != CANCELLED; the web path counts CONFIRMED plus PENDING with lockedUntil > now. The same class can therefore be 'full' on mobile and bookable on web. This divergence is the audit's #1 pattern (dead-parallel implementations) expressed as semantics rather than duplicated code. REQUIRED: reuse the SAME serializable transaction + occupied-seat predicate as app/api/bookings/route.ts - extract it to a shared helper rather than writing a second copy. ACCEPTANCE: two concurrent mobile POSTs for the last seat yield exactly one 2xx and one rejection with exactly one booking in the DB; a class at capacity reports identically on both paths. MUST NOT be closed by review alone - run the concurrency test against the capacity-1 fixture class.
tasks.note: CONN-001 does not close until BOTH T1-01 and T1-12 merge. Do not mark the finding resolved on T1-01 alone.

tasks.title: Build the admin-operated CENTER_ADMIN provisioning path
tasks.acceptance: OWNER DECIDED 2026-08-06: YES - new tutoring centers MUST be onboardable before launch. This is no longer a question, it is a required build, and it is now a launch blocker rather than a P2 curiosity. Context: T1-04's HIDE default removes self-serve CENTER_ADMIN signup on overhaul/16's assumption that a platform ADMIN could still assign the role, which is FALSE (AdminClient.tsx:565 is a table filter; no admin API writes User.role). T1-04 STILL SHIPS AS-IS - self-serve stays hidden - and THIS task supplies the admin-operated path instead. BUILD: an admin-only endpoint that sets User.role to CENTER_ADMIN and links or creates the Center, plus the control in the existing admin users table. THIS IS A PRIVILEGE-ESCALATION SURFACE; every rule below is blocking, not advisory: (1) authorization is re-checked SERVER-SIDE inside the route from the session, never trusted from the client, and reuses the existing requireAdmin pattern from app/api/admin/refund-requests/route.ts - do not write a second admin check (dead-parallel); (2) the role transition is ALLOWLISTED explicitly (STUDENT/TUTOR -> CENTER_ADMIN, and back) - never accept an arbitrary role string from the request body, which would turn this into a way to mint platform ADMINs; (3) this endpoint must NOT be able to grant ADMIN under any input; (4) every call writes an audit row through the existing lib/audit.ts log() with actor, target, previous role and new role - a silent privilege change is unacceptable; (5) rate-limit it like the other sensitive routes. app/admin/** is restricted per overhaul/07 - this task is the explicit grant for exactly the files listed above and nothing else under app/admin/. ACCEPTANCE, all tested by calling the route directly rather than clicking the UI: an ADMIN can promote a STUDENT/TUTOR to CENTER_ADMIN and that user then reaches /centers/[id]/admin; an authenticated TUTOR, an authenticated CENTER_ADMIN, and an anonymous caller each get 403 with NO state change; a body carrying role=ADMIN is rejected; an audit row exists after each successful change. Type E - two review passes, and the second must re-derive the escalation model from scratch instead of confirming the first.

tasks.title: Fix prefix-match open redirect in auth.config.ts redirect callback
tasks.acceptance: OPENED 2026-08-06 by Claude. T1-09 fixed the CLIENT-side callbackUrl guard in app/login/page.tsx and is merged, but auth.config.ts:31-34 independently validates post-login redirects with prefix matching: `if (url.startsWith(baseUrl)) return url`. PROVEN off-origin escapes with baseUrl=https://coursaty.com, 4 of 8 test inputs: 'https://coursaty.com.evil.net/steal' -> origin https://coursaty.com.evil.net; 'https://coursaty.community/steal' -> https://coursaty.community; 'https://coursaty.com@evil.net/' -> https://evil.net (userinfo trick, and it reads as a legitimate link); 'https://coursaty.com.evil.net' -> same off-origin. NOTE the leading-slash inputs ('//evil', '/\evil') are NOT exploitable here, unlike the T1-09 client-side case, because the value is concatenated AFTER baseUrl and stays on-origin - do not copy T1-09's fix verbatim without re-deriving it for this call site. REQUIRED: parse and compare ORIGINS (new URL(url, baseUrl).origin === new URL(baseUrl).origin), never prefix matching. ACCEPTANCE: a table over all 8 inputs above showing 0 off-origin results, committed as a test. Deliberately a SEPARATE branch - do not fold a security fix into an unrelated merge.

tasks.title: Preserve payment-attempt linkage so a superseded Paymob order cannot silently eat money
tasks.acceptance: OPENED 2026-08-06 by Claude on the T1-01 second Type E pass. lib/paymob.ts:157-163 OVERWRITES booking.paymobOrderId on every initiatePayment call, so retrying payment on the same booking orphans the previous Paymob order. The webhook resolves bookings by findFirst({ where: { paymobOrderId } }), which now matches only the newest attempt. If the SUPERSEDED attempt then succeeds, the webhook hits the !booking branch, logs an error and returns 200 - so Paymob stops retrying, the money is captured, and no booking and NO refundReason row exists. That is silent money loss with no audit trail, and unlike the T1-01 race it leaves nothing in the admin refund queue to find it. Not introduced by T1-01 and deliberately NOT folded into it. REQUIRED: a booking may have many payment attempts - model them (PaymentAttempt rows, or at minimum retain prior order ids) and resolve webhooks against the full attempt history, not a single mutable column. Any webhook that cannot be matched to a booking must persist the raw event and raise an alert, never return 200 silently. TOUCHES prisma/schema.prisma (protected, per overhaul/07) - sequence it and do not edit while another task owns that file.
